# Dhammapada (Dhp)
**ID:** Dhp
**Section:** Dhammapada (dhp)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Dhammapada
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/dhp

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Dhammapada* is an ancient verse text of the Khuddaka-nikāya consisting of 423 verses arranged into thematic chapters [SuttaCentral; Hirakawa 1990]. Regarded as one of the oldest texts in the Khuddaka-nikāya, it expresses universal and early Indian ethical wisdom; many of its stanzas are shared with non-Buddhist Indian works, including the *Mahābhārata*, *Manusmṛti*, *Hitopadeśa*, *Garuḍapurāṇa*, and *Yogabhāṣya* [SuttaCentral; Hirakawa 1990; Lamotte 1988]. The text has become one of the most widely read and translated Buddhist scriptures [SuttaCentral; Huber 2008; Sueki 2012]. In the Theravāda tradition it is preserved alongside the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā*, whose traditional attribution to Buddhaghosa has been questioned due to stylistic distinctiveness [Burlingame 1921; Gaffney 2003]. Verses of the *Dhammapada* are also frequently cited in other Pali works, such as the *Jātakanidāna* [Gaffney 2003].
The text circulated widely across various Buddhist schools and languages. Corresponding recensions include the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (traditionally attributed to Dharmatrāta), three manuscripts of a Gāndhārī Dharmapada (including the Dutreuil de Rhins manuscript), the Patna Dharmapada in a mixed Prakrit dialect, Tibetan translations of the *Udānavarga*, and four Chinese translations [Salomon 2018; Lamotte 1988; Nakamura 1980]. SuttaCentral identifies parallels for 425 verses, prominently in the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya and classical Brahmanical texts [SuttaCentral]. These alignments are confirmed by DharmaNexus, which records high-plausibility matches with the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (397 matches), the Patna Dharmapada (392 matches), the Subaši *Udānavarga* (340 matches), and Tibetan *Udānavarga* texts (D0326 and D4099), alongside internal Pali reuse with the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* (890 matches) and the *Vāseṭṭha Sutta* (MN 98 / Snp 3.9) [DharmaNexus].
